five_minutes: RBI announced a massive ₹1 lakh crore OMO bond sale starting September 17, which will drain durable liquidity and push G-sec yields higher.
US CPI inflation at 3.4% and Brent crude holding above $100 have pushed Fed rate hike odds for next week to 90%, tightening global financial conditions.
UK July GDP growth firmed to 0.4% driven by AI services adoption, reducing pressure on the Bank of England for rapid rate cuts.
BRICS finance ministers warned that unilateral trade tariffs threaten global growth, calling for expanded local-currency settlement infrastructure.
SEBI released operational FAQs for its Demat 2.0 tokenised corporate bonds pilot, clarifying custody and audit requirements.

buckets.label: What you need to know today

items.headline: RBI's ₹1 lakh crore OMO bond sale will drain long-term liquidity and push G-sec yields higher
items.what_happened: RBI announced OMO sale auctions of Government of India securities for an aggregate amount of ₹1,00,000 crore in three tranches of ₹50,000 crore, ₹25,000 crore, and ₹25,000 crore starting September 17, 2026.
items.why_it_matters: This durable liquidity absorption will steepen upward pressure on sovereign G-sec yields and further tighten banking system liquidity. Expect money market rates and bank funding costs to rise across maturities.
items.action: Revisit bank funding cost assumptions and monitor G-sec yield curve shifts ahead of the September 17 auction.

items.headline: US CPI inflation at 3.4% and $100 oil push Fed hike probability to 90%, threatening FII flows into India
items.what_happened: US August CPI inflation reached 3.4% year-on-year while Brent crude held above $100 per barrel, driving market probability of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next week to 90%.
items.why_it_matters: Hawkish repricing of US rates strengthens the dollar index and widens US-India interest rate differentials. This heightens FII capital outflow risks from Indian equities and debt while elevating India's imported inflation bill.
items.action: Check portfolio exposure to high-valuation domestic equities vulnerable to institutional FII selling.

items.headline: UK GDP expansion of 0.4% in July firmed further, driven by AI services growth
items.what_happened: Official figures confirmed UK July GDP expanded by 0.4% month-on-month, exceeding analyst forecasts of flat growth, supported by technology and AI adoption across service sectors.
items.why_it_matters: Stronger economic activity reduces pressure on the Bank of England to deliver rapid rate cuts, keeping gilt yields firm and supporting sterling against European peers.

items.headline: BRICS finance ministers warn unilateral tariffs endanger global trade, advocate local currency settlement
items.what_happened: BRICS finance ministers expressed serious concern over unilateral trade barriers and protectionism, urging deeper local-currency trade settlement and interconnected banking infrastructure.
items.why_it_matters: Signals structural fragmentation in global trade channels and long-term momentum toward non-USD settlement mechanisms for cross-border commodity transactions.

items.headline: ECB's Lane signals ongoing inflation monitoring as euro zone growth outlook remains subdued
items.what_happened: ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane outlined the Eurozone economic outlook, emphasizing sticky services inflation despite broader economic growth headwinds.
items.why_it_matters: Confirms the ECB's cautious stance on policy easing, maintaining euro bond yield floors and preventing rapid narrowing of ECB-Fed rate differentials.

items.headline: Persistent global energy price pressures increase risk of renewed rate tightening by major central banks
items.what_happened: Energy cost escalation across major economies is renewing cost-push inflationary pressures, prompting central banks to reassess rate path trajectories.
items.why_it_matters: Sustained high global borrowing costs tighten global liquidity conditions, capping equity earnings multiples and elevating sovereign debt servicing burdens.

items.headline: RBI G-sec auction sets 2033 benchmark yield at 6.81% amid steady market appetite
items.what_happened: RBI auctioned ₹32,000 crore of sovereign bonds, with the 6.57% GS 2033 cutting off at ₹98.36 (6.81% YTM) and the new 2056 paper clearing at a 7.00% yield.
items.why_it_matters: Establishes clear benchmark yield levels across the belly and long end of the Indian sovereign curve prior to the planned OMO liquidity absorption sales.

items.headline: India-Russia $100 billion trade target by 2030 underscores expanding rupee-ruble energy payment mechanisms
items.what_happened: India and Russia announced plans to target $100 billion in bilateral trade by 2030, focusing on critical minerals, nuclear energy, and long-term crude oil deliveries.
items.why_it_matters: Sustained reliance on discounted Russian crude helps limit India's current account deficit expansion, though local currency clearing friction remains an operational hurdle.

items.headline: State government borrowing via RBI WMA facilities rebounds to ₹27,940 crore
items.what_happened: RBI's Weekly Statistical Supplement showed State Government loans and advances under Ways and Means Advances standing at ₹27,940 crore for the week ended September 4, 2026.
items.why_it_matters: Highlights widening short-term fiscal mismatches among Indian states, pointing to sustained supply pressures in upcoming State Development Loan (SDL) bond auctions.

items.headline: SEBI advances Demat 2.0 pilot for tokenised corporate bonds with operational FAQ release
items.what_happened: SEBI issued comprehensive FAQs following the successful pilot launch of Demat 2.0 to clarify technical, custody, and settlement workflows for tokenised corporate debt securities.
items.why_it_matters: Clarifies regulatory compliance and audit trail requirements for corporate bond tokenisation, establishing primary operational standards for issuers and clearing members.
items.action: Review SEBI FAQ operational guidelines for client corporate debt custody and audit compliance.

items.headline: RBI updates Priority Sector Lending classification rules for banks and NBFCs
items.what_happened: RBI issued the Priority Sector Lending Third Amendment Directions 2026, revising sub-target compliance classifications and reporting criteria for lenders.
items.why_it_matters: Bank and NBFC audit and compliance teams must update PSL portfolio classification checks and shortfall penalty calculations under the amended directions.
items.action: Verify PSL sub-target compliance matrices for bank and NBFC audit clients against the Third Amendment guidelines.

items.headline: RBI rationalises FEMA circulars to streamline cross-border compliance for Authorised Persons
items.what_happened: RBI issued A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 21 consolidating and rationalising existing regulatory circulars under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
items.why_it_matters: Simplifies operational cross-border remittance rules, non-resident account compliance, and regulatory filing requirements for corporate advisory and CA practices.
items.action: Review updated FEMA circular consolidation for client cross-border transaction compliance.

items.headline: RBI updates guidelines for non-resident bank accounts held with Authorised Dealers
items.what_happened: RBI issued circular directions modifying rules governing rupee and foreign currency accounts maintained by non-resident banks with AD Category-I banks in India.
items.why_it_matters: Impacts correspondent banking audit checks, VOSTRO account balances, and cross-border bank reconciliation procedures for institutional clients.

items.headline: RBI announces ₹5 lakh crore overnight VRRR auction as banking liquidity stays tight
items.what_happened: RBI scheduled a 1-day Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction of ₹5,00,000 crore for September 15, 2026, to manage short-term system liquidity distribution.
items.why_it_matters: Reflects RBI's active fine-tuning of overnight money market rates near the policy repo rate ahead of larger structural liquidity drains via OMO sales.
